name: readlink
synopsis: ssize_t readlink(const char *restrict pathname, char *restrict buf, size_t bufsiz);
ssize_t readlinkat(int dirfd, const char *restrict pathname, char *restrict buf, size_t bufsiz);
description: The readlink() function reads the contents of a symbolic link specified by pathname into the buffer buf of size bufsiz, without appending a null terminator and truncating if necessary. The readlinkat() variant performs the same operation but interprets relative pathnames relative to the directory referred to by dirfd.

parameters.name: buf
parameters.description: Buffer to store the contents of the symbolic link

parameters.name: dirfd
parameters.description: Directory file descriptor for relative paths (applies to readlinkat)

return_value.success: Returns the number of bytes placed in buf (may indicate truncation if equal to bufsiz)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Search permission is denied for a component of the path prefix
pathname is relative but dirfd is neither AT_FDCWD nor a valid file descriptor (for readlinkat)
buf extends outside the process’s allocated address space
bufsiz is not positive or the named file is not a symbolic link
An I/O error occurred while reading from the filesystem
Too many symbolic links were encountered in translating the pathname
A pathname, or a component of a pathname, was too long
The named file does not exist
A component of the path prefix is not a directory, or (for readlinkat) pathname is relative and dirfd is not a directory

versions: readlink() from 4.4BSD and POSIX.1-2001; readlinkat() from Linux 2.6.16 and glibc 2.4
